India make best start to Olympic shooting cycle in decades 
 Edited by Hijam Raju Singh / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 16, 2026, 15:25 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Jaypal Malviya NEW DELHI: India have made their strongest start to an Olympic qualification cycle in shooting in at least 16 years, securing three quota places for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics at the ISSF World Championship Rifle/Pistol/Shotgun in Doha, Qatar. For the first time across five consecutive Olympic cycles, stretching from London 2012 to LA28, Indian shooters have secured three Olympic quotas at the very first qualification event. The landmark achievement, made possible by podium finishes across all three shooting disciplines — rifle, pistol and shotgun — has given India an early advantage in the race for Olympic berths. Watch Kynan Chenai: The 38-Year-Old Gun Barrel, Asian Games Gold and the LA 2028 Dream | TOISA Spotlight Jaypal Malviya opened India's account with a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event. Niraj Kumar followed with bronze in the men's 50m rifle 3 positions, before Vivaan Kapoor completed the impressive haul with silver in the men's trap. The three podium finishes not only secured India's first Olympic quotas for LA28 but also underlined the growing depth across the country's shooting programme. Three LA 2028 quotas at first attempt 
 India's Doha performance represents a significant improvement on its opening-event returns in the previous four Olympic qualification cycles. The country secured two quotas at the 2010 Munich World Championships ahead of London 2012, followed by just one at the 2014 Granada World Championships before the Rio 2016 Games. The tally improved to two at the 2018 Changwon World Championships ahead of Tokyo 2020, while India collected two quotas from the 2022 Osijek Shotgun World Championships and Cairo Rifle/Pistol World Championships before Paris 2024. The three quotas in Doha in 2026 have therefore set a new benchmark for India's opening performance in an Olympic qualification campaign since the London 2012 cycle. Welcoming the achievement, National Rifle Association of India (NRAI) president Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo said: "Starting an Olympic cycle with three quotas right at the first World Championship is a huge boost for everyone involved. What makes me happiest is that all three disciplines—rifle, pistol and shotgun—delivered podium finishes. Usually, it takes a few World Cups for the momentum to build, so getting three spots on the board this early takes a lot of pressure off the team and gives our coaching staff a clear runway to plan for Los Angeles. " NRAI secretary general Pawankumar Singh also praised the shooters for delivering under pressure against a strong international field. "Winning a quota at a World Championship is never easy because every top shooter in the world is competing in the same field. Jaypal, Niraj and Vivaan kept their composure in very tight finals and earned those spots the hard way. Our high-performance team and coaches put in months of quiet work behind the scenes to get us here, and we will keep building on this start over the next two years," he said. Join conversation

 India also finished second in the overall medal standings in Doha with 13 medals, comprising two gold, seven silver and four bronze, further underlining the strength of its campaign. Indian shooters dominate ISSF People's Choice Awards race
 India's impressive showing in international shooting has extended beyond the competition arena, with the country's shooters emerging as frontrunners in the ISSF 2026 Athlete of the Year People's Choice Awards. Four Indian shooters — Esha Singh, Elavenil Valarivan, Tilottama Sen and Sakshi Padekar — feature among the five nominees in the women's category, while Tushar Mane is leading the men's voting. Voting, which began on November 9, will close on November 18, with the winners in the men's and women's categories to be announced thereafter.
